description.narrative:
Oxfam has worked to address poverty and inequality in Nigeria since the 1960’s. Our vision is for a Nigeria without inequality and poverty, and where every voice counts. Our mission is to strengthen and empower civil society to help shape a Nigeria without inequality and poverty. Under the new country operating strategy, Oxfam in Nigeria is focused and aligned with the Oxfam confederation’s global strategic framework to achieve just economies, gender justice, and accountable governance. This latter goalaims to realize ‘anactive and engaged civil society that is able to help strengthen governance, transparency and accountability in the public and private sectors and amplify voices in the fight for climate justice’. Furthermore, communities and CSOs willnot only be empowered to lead climate-resilient livelihoods but to also challenge governments and the private sector to transition from business-as-usual approaches to climate-resilient economic development and business activities. However, there is a general lack of accountability and transparency in the governance systems across Nigeria and this makes it extremely difficult for citizens to be aware of or able to influence the resource flows of government agencies, and big businesses such as multinational companies operating in the extractives and large conglomerates.
Oxfam in Nigeria will draw on its long history of working with communities, the government (at various levels) and the private sector to promote improved governance and accountability.In 2017, it supported the national government’s developmentprocess of the National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights in Nigeria (NAP). These plans are developed to demonstrate the state’s commitment to protecting human rights as they relate to business activities, along three pillars of respect, protection, and remediation. Replacing the previous NAP that expired in late 2013, the draft NAP 2021-25 remains under review, after several lengthy stakeholder consultation and validation periods. In August 2021, Nigeria signed into law a suite of legislative and regulatory changes aiming to reform its oil and gas sector, with the passage of the Petroleum Industry Act, 2020 (PIA). Among administrative and fiscal framework changes, several funds were created including those to address negative impacts on communities and environmental remediation. However, the implementation of these complex set of reforms necessitates detailed tracking to ensure accountability, transparency, and environmental justice, especially as the country concurrently initiates “The Decade of Gas” development plans.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
